summary: Godot is a free and open source game engine published under the MIT licence; the current stable release is 4.7.2, announced on 18 August 2026, in the 4.7 feature line released on 18 June 2026. It covers the build side of a world well: rendering on Vulkan, Direct3D 12, Metal or OpenGL, rigid and soft body physics, positioned audio, animation and skeletons, its own scripting language, and packaging for desktop, mobile, browsers and headsets. Its distinctive idea is that everything is a node in a tree, any tree can be saved as a scene, and any saved scene can be placed inside another scene as though it were a single node, with per-instance property changes layered on top. It reads and writes the common model transfer format from Khronos, but the files it actually authors in are its own text and binary scene files, which no other runtime reads. Unusually among open engines it ships a working multiplayer layer with property replication, spawned-object replication and per-object authority, and it reaches headsets through the cross-vendor immersive runtime interface built into the engine core, plus the browser immersive interface on web builds; it has nothing for identity, rights, world naming, portals between worlds or anchors shared between devices. The point a standards audience should hold on to is that almost every subsystem sits behind a public server or extension interface, so a gap in Godot is usually a gap in the default build rather than a locked door: the physics engine, the model-format extension set, and extra rendering passes can all be replaced or added from outside without forking the engine.

coverage.note: Three rendering methods ship in the engine: Forward+ using clustered lighting for desktop, Mobile using traditional single-pass forward lighting, and Compatibility using non-clustered forward. All three are forward renderers; the documentation has a section explaining why deferred rendering is not used. There is no public render graph interface, though one exists internally.

coverage.note: Forward+ and Mobile go through RenderingDevice onto Vulkan, Direct3D 12 or Metal; Compatibility uses OpenGL, meaning OpenGL ES 3.0, desktop OpenGL 3.3, or WebGL 2.0 in the browser. Two details matter for a standards audience: the Direct3D 12 driver is still documented as experimental in 4.7, while the Metal driver is native and now uses Metal 4; and there is no WebGPU backend, which is the reason the advanced renderers cannot run on the web at all.

coverage.note: Cameras register themselves with the nearest viewport and exactly one is current at a time, with perspective, orthogonal and offset-frustum projections. In an immersive session the pose comes from the headset instead: XRCamera3D positions itself from tracking data under a tracking-space origin node, and most of its properties are then overridden by the active immersive interface.

coverage.note: The whole engine is built on it: nodes form a tree, a tree with a single root is a scene, and a saved scene can be instantiated inside another scene and then behaves like one node. This is Godot's central idea and the reason it has no separate prefab concept.

For authoring it uses its own formats, tscn and scn for scenes and tres and res for resources, and no other runtime reads those.

coverage.note: Skeleton3D holds the bone hierarchy, a Skin binds a mesh to it, and BoneAttachment3D hangs other nodes off a named bone; skeletons come in through glTF import.

sources.quote: A node that dynamically copies or overrides the 3D transform of a bone in its parent Skeleton3D.

coverage.note: Meshes carry blend shapes, imported from glTF morph targets, and each shape's weight can be read and set at runtime on the mesh instance.

sources.title: MeshInstance3D - Godot Engine (stable) documentation

sources.title: MultiMeshInstance3D - Godot Engine (stable) documentation

coverage.note: Layering by reference works: an instanced scene keeps a live link to its source file, per-instance property changes override the source, and Editable Children opens the instance's inner nodes for local edits. What is missing against the definition is composition from several sources at once with declared strength ordering, the way a layered scene description format does it; a Godot node has exactly one source scene.

sources.title: Creating instances - Godot Engine (stable) documentation
sources.quote: Changing a property on an instance always overrides values from the corresponding packed scene.

coverage.note: One unit is one metre and the engine states plainly that physics and everything else are tuned for that scale.

coverage.note: The glTF exporter carries exactly one asset-header field bearing on rights: a free-text copyright string, written on export when it is non-empty and read back on import. That states who claims an asset; it does not state what a recipient may do with it, and nothing reads it at the point of use. Import metadata otherwise records import settings only. Correction: an earlier version of this row said nothing survives a glTF export. That was wrong - the copyright string does.

sources.quote: The copyright string in the asset header of the glTF file. This is set during import if present and export if non-empty.

coverage.note: The only authorship-adjacent field anywhere in the transfer path is the free-text copyright string in the glTF asset header. It is unsigned, so it records a claim rather than proving one. There is no signing, no key material and no content credential in the asset pipeline.

sources.title: GLTFState - Godot Engine (stable) documentation
sources.quote: The copyright string in the asset header of the glTF file. This is set during import if present and export if non-empty.

coverage.note: SkeletonProfileHumanoid defines a fixed 56-bone humanoid layout in four groups and exists, in the engine's own words, for standardization. sources.title: BoneAttachment3D - Godot Engine (stable) documentation
sources.quote: This node selects a bone in a Skeleton3D and attaches to it.

coverage.note: Generic mesh level of detail and visibility ranges apply to avatar meshes like any other, but there is no avatar-aware reduction, no crowd imposter and no agreed reduced avatar representation.

sources.title: Mesh level of detail (LOD) - Godot Engine (stable) documentation
sources.quote: Mesh LOD works with any node that draws 3D meshes.

coverage.note: RigidBody3D, StaticBody3D, AnimatableBody3D and CharacterBody3D cover the usual cases. Two engines ship: the built-in Godot Physics and Jolt Physics, added in 4.4, which new projects use by default and which is chosen with one project setting. A third engine can be substituted entirely from outside, because PhysicsServer3D is a public interface with an extension point.

sources.title: PhysicsServer3DExtension - Godot Engine (stable) documentation
sources.quote: Intended for use with GDExtension to create custom implementations of PhysicsServer3D.

coverage.note: Collision shapes are separate child nodes from the visible mesh, covering box, sphere, capsule, cylinder, convex hull and concave triangle mesh, with documented advice on the cost of each.

sources.title: Collision shapes (3D) - Godot Engine (stable) documentation
sources.quote: Concave shapes are the slowest option but are also the most accurate in Godot.

coverage.note: Pin, hinge, slider, cone twist and generic six-degree-of-freedom joints all exist. The gap is between the two engines: under Jolt a number of joint properties, mainly the soft limit settings, are not supported, so the same scene can behave differently depending on which engine is selected.

sources.title: Using Jolt Physics - Godot Engine (stable) documentation
sources.quote: there are a number of joint properties that are not supported, mainly ones related to configuring the joint's soft limits

coverage.note: PhysicsMaterial carries friction and bounce with rough and absorbent flags controlling how two surfaces combine.

sources.title: PhysicsMaterial - Godot Engine (stable) documentation
sources.quote: Holds physics-related properties of a surface, namely its roughness and bounciness.

coverage.note: There is a fixed physics tick rate, but no claim anywhere in the documentation that the same inputs give the same result on two machines, and the engine states that ordinary floating point maths is not guaranteed to be exact. Anyone planning lockstep or rollback networking on Godot has to prove determinism themselves.

sources.title: float - Godot Engine (stable) documentation

sources.title: SoftBody3D - Godot Engine (stable) documentation
sources.quote: A deformable 3D physics mesh. Used to create elastic or deformable objects such as cloth, rubber

coverage.note: Area3D is a region that reports bodies and other areas entering and leaving, and can also override gravity, damping and the audio bus inside itself.

sources.title: Area3D - Godot Engine (stable) documentation
sources.quote: Emitted when the received body enters this area.

coverage.note: AudioStreamPlayer3D places a sound in the world with a choice of inverse, inverse square, logarithmic or no distance attenuation, plus unit size and maximum distance.

sources.title: AudioStreamPlayer3D - Godot Engine (stable) documentation
sources.quote: Plays audio with positional sound effects, based on the relative position of the audio listener.

coverage.note: Direction is rendered by panning between output channels, with a per-node panning strength over a project-wide setting. There is no head-related transfer function and no ambisonic path in the engine, so binaural rendering has to come from an add-on or the platform.

sources.title: AudioStreamPlayer3D - Godot Engine (stable) documentation
sources.quote: Scales the panning strength for this node

coverage.note: Reverb is real and routable: buses carry effects in order, and an Area3D can send the sounds inside it to a named reverb bus with an amount and a uniformity. What is missing is any acoustic model of the room itself; the reverb is authored, not derived from geometry.

sources.title: Area3D - Godot Engine (stable) documentation
sources.quote: The name of the reverb bus to use for this area's associated audio.

sources.title: Audio buses - Godot Engine (stable) documentation
sources.quote: Audio buses can contain all sorts of effects. These effects modify the sound in one way or another and are applied in order.

coverage.note: There is a low-pass attenuation filter on each 3D sound, but it is driven by distance and by area masks, not by geometry between source and listener. Real occlusion has to be scripted with ray casts that drive that filter.

sources.title: AudioStreamPlayer3D - Godot Engine (stable) documentation
sources.quote: The cutoff frequency of the attenuation low-pass filter, in Hz.

coverage.note: Audio streams are local resources loaded from the project or from disk. Nothing in the engine delivers audio over a network at scale; on web builds the playback type setting only chooses between browser samples and streaming inside the page.

sources.title: Audio streams - Godot Engine (stable) documentation
sources.quote: It exists so Web exports use Web Audio-API based samples instead of streaming all sounds to the browser.

coverage.note: No voice transport ships. AudioEffectCapture hands a project raw samples off a bus and the documentation names network transmission as a use for it, but the codec, the jitter buffer and the transport are all the developer's problem.

sources.title: AudioEffectCapture - Godot Engine (stable) documentation
sources.quote: Exposes audio samples from an audio bus in real-time, such that it can be accessed as data.

coverage.note: This is the part that is unusual for an open engine. MultiplayerSynchronizer replicates a declared list of properties from the authority to remote peers on a configurable interval or on change, and MultiplayerSpawner replicates the creation and removal of nodes. Remote procedure calls with reliability and ordering modes sit alongside it.

sources.title: MultiplayerSynchronizer - Godot Engine (stable) documentation
sources.quote: Synchronizes properties from the multiplayer authority to the remote peers.

sources.title: MultiplayerSpawner - Godot Engine (stable) documentation
sources.quote: automatically replicates spawnable nodes from the authority to other multiplayer peers

coverage.note: Every node has a multiplayer authority, the server by default, settable per node; remote calls can be restricted to the authority or opened to any peer.

sources.title: High-level multiplayer - Godot Engine (stable) documentation
sources.quote: Only the multiplayer authority can call remotely. The authority is the server by default

coverage.note: Per-synchronizer visibility can be set for a peer directly or computed by visibility filter callbacks, which is the mechanism for sending each client only what it needs. The policy is entirely the developer's: there is no spatial partition, no area of interest and no automatic culling by distance.

sources.title: MultiplayerSynchronizer - Godot Engine (stable) documentation
sources.quote: Adds a peer visibility filter for this synchronizer

coverage.note: No client-side prediction, reconciliation or rollback in the engine. Replication is authority to peer, and the multiplayer guide names client-side prediction as something a project has to add. Searched the Godot 4.7 stable documentation search index (1,591 pages, including the class reference) for predict, rollback, reconcili and netcod on 2026-10-19; rollback, reconcili and netcod have no match, and the only networking page that mentions prediction is the high-level multiplayer guide quoted here.

sources.title: High-level multiplayer - Godot Engine (stable) documentation
sources.quote: This comes with some tradeoffs (such as server-side performance and complexity due to the need for client-side prediction), but will make it much harder for attackers to cheat by sending falsified data.

coverage.note: Three peers ship behind one interface: ENet over UDP for native builds, WebSocket, and WebRTC data channels. A project can add its own peer implementation.

sources.title: High-level multiplayer - Godot Engine (stable) documentation
sources.quote: ENetMultiplayerPeer, one based on WebRTC (WebRTCMultiplayerPeer), and one based on WebSocket (WebSocketMultiplayerPeer)

sources.title: ENetMultiplayerPeer - Godot Engine (stable) documentation
sources.quote: ENet only uses UDP, not TCP.

coverage.note: The WebRTC integration exposes data channels only; there is no audio or video track handling, and no media transport of any kind in the engine.

sources.title: WebRTCPeerConnection - Godot Engine (stable) documentation
sources.quote: A WebRTC connection between the local computer and a remote peer.

coverage.note: Joining is covered inside one application: a peer connects, an optional authentication callback can hold it in an authenticating state until the project completes or times out the handshake, and spawners bring the joiner up to date. There is no standard for what that handshake contains and no cross-operator session concept.

sources.title: SceneMultiplayer - Godot Engine (stable) documentation
sources.quote: The callback to execute when receiving authentication data sent via send_auth().

coverage.note: Nothing for leaving one world and arriving in another with state intact. Changing scene inside one application is not the same thing and does not cross an operator boundary: the outgoing scene is removed from the tree and then freed, so nothing carries across unless the project saves and reloads it by hand.

sources.title: SceneTree - Godot Engine (stable) documentation
sources.quote: The current scene node is immediately removed from the tree.

coverage.note: Inside one session the server can notify clients of other peers connecting and disconnecting, which gives a roster. Across operators there is nothing.

sources.title: SceneMultiplayer - Godot Engine (stable) documentation
sources.quote: notifies clients of other peers' connection/disconnection, and relays messages between them

sources.title: ENetMultiplayerPeer - Godot Engine (stable) documentation
sources.quote: create_client()

sources.title: ENetMultiplayerPeer - Godot Engine (stable) documentation
sources.quote: Create client that connects to a server at address using specified port.

coverage.note: There is a fixed physics tick and a Time singleton, but the singleton reads the local machine's own clock and converts between formats. There is no shared clock, no offset estimation and no agreed event ordering across peers, so two peers can disagree and nothing in the engine reconciles them.

sources.title: Time - Godot Engine (stable) documentation
sources.quote: The Time singleton allows converting time between various formats and also getting time information from the system.

coverage.note: A game engine, not an identity provider. The only identifier the engine issues is a peer number handed out at connection time: the server is always 1 and every client gets a random positive integer. It is scoped to one session and means nothing outside it.

sources.title: High-level multiplayer - Godot Engine (stable) documentation
sources.quote: Every peer is assigned a unique ID. The server's ID is always 1, and clients are assigned a random positive integer.

sources.quote: If the Callable is empty (default), peers will be automatically accepted as soon as they connect.

Anchors can be made persistent so they come back in the right place next time the application starts, if the runtime supports it. Sharing anchors between devices is stated as not supported, which the docs attribute to the spatial entities specification rather than to Godot.

sources.quote: Sharing of anchors is currently not supported in the spatial entities specification.
